perception.note: Low light vision, Scent 60ft imprecise, Tremorsense 40ft imprecise

generalAbilities.name: Studded Cheeks
generalAbilities.description: The cave squirrel can store up to six gems in its cheeks. It typically begins combat with all six, and it loses a gem each time it uses gem spit.

defensiveAbilities.name: Defensive Scream
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger The cave squirrel rolls initiative or has taken damage before initiative

Effect The cave squirrel lets out an ear-piercing shriek, alerting any other cave squirrels in the area to its plight. It uses Screaming Force.

offensiveAbilities.name: Concussive Gem
offensiveAbilities.description: On a critical hit on a gem spit Strike, the target must succeed at a DC 22 Fortitude Saving Throw save or become Stunned 1.

offensiveAbilities.name: Forage for Gems
offensiveAbilities.description: The cave squirrel dives underground in search of gems. The cave squirrel Burrows up to its Speed. It must end its movement back on the surface. During its burrow, it happens upon 1d4 #gems cheap gems (such as salt or quartz), which it stuffs in its cheeks, up to its maximum of 6.

offensiveAbilities.name: Natural Speed
offensiveAbilities.description: A cave squirrel isn't affected by difficult terrain from earth or stone.

offensiveAbilities.name: Screaming Force
offensiveAbilities.description: The cave squirrel lets out a terrible scream. Non–cave squirrel creatures within 30 feet must succeed at a DC 22 Fortitude Saving Throw save or take 2d10 Sonic Damage damage. On a critical failure, a creature is Deafened for 1 minute. The cave squirrel can't use Screaming Force again for 1d4 rounds.

offensiveAbilities.name: Grab
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.
